subsystems.name: Design software
subsystems.role: chooses which protein shapes fit together into a repeating grid.

subsystems.name: Building blocks
subsystems.role: the repeat unit — a folded protein or small protein domain with sticky patches on its faces.

subsystems.name: Assembly control
subsystems.role: decides whether units form a flat sheet, a tube, a cage or a 3D crystal.

subsystems.name: Production host
subsystems.role: makes the designed protein in quantity.

subsystems.name: Purification and formulation
subsystems.role: isolates clean protein and triggers assembly under controlled conditions.

subsystems.name: Characterisation
subsystems.role: checks the real lattice matches the design.

subsystems.name: Bulk consolidation
subsystems.role: turns nanoscale lattices into a usable solid.

buildSteps.title: Choose a target geometry
buildSteps.detail: Decide the symmetry and spacing of the grid, for example a flat hexagonal sheet or a cubic lattice a few nanometres across.

buildSteps.title: Design the interface
buildSteps.detail: Work out which surfaces could join two copies of the protein, using shape complementarity and buried hydrophobic area.

buildSteps.title: Specify the sequence
buildSteps.detail: Generative models such as ProteinMPNN propose amino-acid sequences that fold to the intended shape and present the right sticky face.

buildSteps.title: Filter in silico
buildSteps.detail: Structure predictors and physics-based scoring reject sequences that misfold, aggregate or assemble the wrong way; only a few per cent usually pass.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the gene
buildSteps.detail: Order a codon-optimised DNA sequence and clone it into an expression plasmid.

buildSteps.title: Express and purify
buildSteps.detail: Grow the host organism, induce protein production, break the cells open and purify the protein to high purity.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and anneal
buildSteps.detail: Adjust buffer, temperature and sometimes metal ions so the units slowly click into a regular lattice rather than a tangled aggregate.

buildSteps.title: Verify the structure
buildSteps.detail: Image the lattice at atomic resolution to confirm the design matched the reality; failures feed back into the design loop.

buildSteps.title: Consolidate into a material
buildSteps.detail: Crosslink or densify the lattice to make a self-standing film, fibre or composite, then measure stiffness and strength.

prerequisites.why: designers need to know the shape a sequence will adopt before making it.
tools like ProteinMPNN generate workable sequences where manual design was hopeless.
each design is a new gene, so hundreds of candidates must be ordered and tested.
gram-scale material needs far more protein than a typical lab prep yields.
no established route exists to spin or mould designed proteins into bulk structural parts.
strength and toughness of a lattice cannot yet be reliably predicted from its sequence.

pathway.milestone: nanoscale designed lattices and 2D arrays built and imaged in the lab
pathway.unlocks: proof that scratch-built proteins can self-assemble into ordered grids.

pathway.milestone: lattices used as functional platforms — antigen display for vaccines, enzyme scaffolding, template for inorganic materials
pathway.unlocks: a market that funds the design toolkit before structural use matures.

pathway.milestone: designed protein fibres and films with tunable stiffness, made at litre scale
pathway.unlocks: competing with spider-silk-like materials in textiles and medical implants.

pathway.milestone: consolidated protein composites as structural material
pathway.unlocks: light, degradable alternatives to some plastics and composites — if strength, water resistance and cost can be solved.
